hypotheses.title: Nanobody CDR3 Arg-fork salt bridge to p6 Asp
hypotheses.scaffold_rationale: De novo VHH-like single domain (~110-125 aa) with no TCR or natural binder template; long CDR3 can descend into the MHC groove while framework contacts the alpha2 helix.
hypotheses.target_surface: Peptide p5 Ala-p8 Val, especially p6 Asp side-chain carboxylate (OD1/OD2), plus the top of the HLA-A*11 alpha2 helix.
hypotheses.mechanism: CDR3 tip places an Arg guanidinium within salt-bridge/H-bond distance of the p6 Asp carboxylate, with an adjacent Ser/Thr H-bonding to the same carboxylate; CDR1/CDR2 pack against alpha2 residues to position the loop. Hydrophobic CDR3 side chains contact p7 Gly/p8 Val.
hypotheses.discrimination_hypothesis: The WT peptide has Gly at p6, so it lacks the carboxylate required to satisfy the buried Arg; the resulting unsatisfied charge and empty pocket make WT binding strongly disfavored, whereas G12D provides the complementary Asp.
hypotheses.peptide_dependence_hypothesis: The highest-affinity contacts are to p6-p8 and the peptide-dependent groove conformation; without peptide, those contacts and the stabilized groove surface are absent.
hypotheses.generation_plan: De novo CDR3 motif design with RFantibody/RFdiffusion, sequence optimization with ProteinMPNN, and filtering by AlphaFold2/Chai or Boltz structure and interface metrics.
failure_modes: Arg may remain solvent-exposed rather than forming the intended salt bridge
CDR3 may not adopt the designed conformation in the actual VHH framework
WT may still bind through backbone H-bonds if the Arg is not sufficiently buried
Nanobody may express poorly or aggregate
hypotheses.risk: medium: strong chemical specificity mechanism, but loop conformation and electrostatic desolvation are uncertain

hypotheses.title: De novo miniprotein with an Asp-binding pocket and peptide clamp
hypotheses.scaffold_rationale: A 55-85 aa de novo helical bundle designed against the pMHC surface, with no natural binder derivation; concave pocket plus flanking helices provide both affinity and shape complementarity.
hypotheses.target_surface: Peptide p4 Gly-p8 Val and flanking tops of alpha1 and alpha2 helices, with the pocket centered on p6 Asp.
hypotheses.mechanism: A pocket lined by Arg/Lys plus Asn/Ser forms a desolvated H-bond network to the p6 Asp carboxylate; adjacent hydrophobic residues clamp p5 Ala and p8 Val; scaffold helices pack against groove helices for orientation.
hypotheses.discrimination_hypothesis: Pocket charge and geometry are matched to an Asp side chain; WT p6 Gly cannot fill the pocket or neutralize the basic residue, creating an unsatisfied charge and steric/energetic penalty.
hypotheses.peptide_dependence_hypothesis: The clamp and pocket include direct contacts to peptide atoms p5-p8; apo HLA lacks these atoms and the peptide-stabilized groove, so the designed interface cannot form.
hypotheses.generation_plan: Target-conditioned RFdiffusion against the pMHC complex, ProteinMPNN sequence design, then AlphaFold2/Chai or Boltz validation with negative-design scoring against WT and apo complexes.
failure_modes: Designed pocket may collapse or fail to desolvate the Arg-Asp pair
WT binding may occur if hydrophobic contacts dominate over the Asp-specific pocket
Apo HLA may present a partially compatible empty groove
hypotheses.risk: medium-high: best opportunity for true de novo specificity, but pocket preorganization is difficult

hypotheses.title: scFv with electrostatic CDR-H3 and hydrophobic CDR-L3
hypotheses.scaffold_rationale: De novo VH-VL single chain (~240-250 aa) with no natural binder derivation; CDR-H3 provides mutation-specific electrostatic recognition while CDR-L3 provides peptide-context affinity.
hypotheses.target_surface: Peptide p6 Asp-p8 Val and the alpha1 helix top, especially p6 side chain and p8 Val side chain.
hypotheses.mechanism: CDR-H3 contains an Arg that forms a salt bridge to p6 Asp carboxylate; CDR-L3 packs a hydrophobic residue against p8 Val; framework/CDR contacts to alpha1 orient the Fv. The combined contact set requires both the mutant side chain and peptide context.
hypotheses.discrimination_hypothesis: WT p6 Gly cannot form the CDR-H3 salt bridge, and without that anchor the CDR-L3 hydrophobic contact alone is insufficient for detectable binding.
hypotheses.peptide_dependence_hypothesis: CDR-L3 contacts p8 Val and CDR-H3 contacts p6 Asp; both are peptide atoms absent in apo HLA, and empty MHC lacks the peptide-dependent groove conformation.
hypotheses.generation_plan: De novo Fv design with RFantibody or target-conditioned diffusion, CDR sequence optimization with ProteinMPNN, and validation by AlphaFold2/Chai plus WT/apo counter-screens.
failure_modes: scFv may misfold or aggregate due to VH-VL pairing uncertainty
CDR loops may not match the designed geometry
WT may retain weak binding through hydrophobic CDR-L3 contacts
Linker length or orientation may prevent simultaneous H3/L3 contacts
hypotheses.risk: high: two-domain complexity and loop uncertainty, but strong potential for affinity plus specificity

hypotheses.title: Short beta-hairpin peptide reader with an Arg tip
hypotheses.scaffold_rationale: A 30-45 aa de novo beta-hairpin, small enough to insert between alpha1 and alpha2; no natural binder or TCR template. Its strand backbone can H-bond to peptide backbone while the tip reads p6 Asp.
hypotheses.target_surface: Peptide backbone p5-p8 and p6 Asp side chain, with flanking contacts to groove helices.
hypotheses.mechanism: The hairpin tip Arg forms a salt bridge to p6 Asp; adjacent strand residues H-bond to peptide backbone carbonyl/amide groups; hydrophobic side chains on the opposite face pack against groove helices.
hypotheses.discrimination_hypothesis: The Arg tip requires the p6 Asp carboxylate; WT Gly cannot satisfy it, and the backbone H-bond network is only productive when the mutant side chain anchors the hairpin.
hypotheses.peptide_dependence_hypothesis: Strand backbone H-bonds are to peptide atoms p5-p8; apo HLA lacks these atoms, so the hairpin has no peptide anchor and should not bind.
hypotheses.generation_plan: Motif scaffolding with RFdiffusion for the Arg-Asp salt bridge and peptide backbone H-bonds, sequence design with ProteinMPNN, and stability filtering with AlphaFold2/Chai.
failure_modes: Short beta-hairpin may be unstable or unstructured in solution
Arg tip may fail to reach p6 Asp without clashing with groove helices
Backbone H-bonds may be satisfied by solvent instead of peptide
WT may still permit hairpin binding through backbone contacts alone
hypotheses.risk: high: minimal scaffold gives clear specificity logic but low stability and affinity ceiling
